reason: An attached head carries the row's freshness (valid_until, stale, pending); a bare head has no row and so no such keys. The values are checked by the freshness tests, the diff only allows the keys to exist on the subject.
An attached panel payload opens with the same head as the manifest, so it carries valid_until, stale and pending too; a bare payload has no row to take them from.
The attached freshness map answers from the published row and adds the reader's stale verdict to each panel entry; a bare cockpit has no row and reports only as_of and status.

An attached etag hashes the row's body hash with stale, pending and the row count; a bare one hashes the content fragments, so equal content gives different tags by design. Only that both sides are a tag is held here.

The payload's etag is the head's etag and differs by construction for the same reason as the manifest's: the attached one is built from the row's body hash and freshness, the bare one from the content.
The manifest etag hashes the panels' heads, whose etags differ by construction between a row-built head and a content-built one, so the manifest etag differs for the same reason.
